cards.front: What pulmonary function pattern defines restrictive lung disease, and how does DLCO help find the cause?
cards.back: **TLC is low**. FEV1 and FVC both fall, so **FEV1/FVC is normal or high**. **DLCO is low** in interstitial (intrinsic) disease and usually **normal** in extrinsic causes such as obesity, neuromuscular weakness or kyphoscoliosis.
cards.back_pt: A **CPT está baixa**. VEF1 e CVF caem juntos, então a **relação VEF1/CVF fica normal ou alta**. A **DLCO está baixa** na doença intersticial (intrínseca) e geralmente **normal** nas causas extrínsecas, como obesidade, fraqueza neuromuscular ou cifoescoliose.

cards.front: What is the histologic pattern of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis?
cards.back: **Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP)**: patchy fibrosis of different ages, with **fibroblastic foci** next to areas of normal lung. It is worst in the **subpleural, basal** regions and ends in **honeycombing**.
cards.back_pt: **Pneumonia intersticial usual (PIU)**: fibrose em placas, de idades diferentes, com **focos fibroblásticos** ao lado de áreas de pulmão normal. Predomina nas regiões **subpleurais e basais** e evolui para **faveolamento** (*honeycombing*).

cards.front: Why does silicosis increase the risk of tuberculosis?
cards.back: Silica particles taken up by **alveolar macrophages** damage their **phagolysosomes**. The macrophages can no longer kill mycobacteria well, so **tuberculosis** (new or reactivated) becomes more likely.
cards.back_pt: As partículas de sílica fagocitadas pelos **macrófagos alveolares** lesam seus **fagolisossomos**. Os macrófagos passam a matar mal as micobactérias, e a **tuberculose** (nova ou reativada) fica mais provável.

cards.front: Which lung zone, histologic marker and pleural finding point to asbestos exposure?
cards.back: Fibrosis of the **lower lobes**. **Ferruginous bodies**: golden-brown, beaded rods (asbestos fibers coated with iron and protein). **Calcified pleural plaques**, often on the parietal pleura and diaphragm.
cards.back_pt: Fibrose dos **lobos inferiores**. **Corpos ferruginosos**: bastões castanho-dourados, em contas (fibras de asbesto revestidas de ferro e proteína). **Placas pleurais calcificadas**, geralmente na pleura parietal e no diafragma.

cards.front: What lesion does chronic beryllium disease cause, and who is exposed?
cards.back: **Noncaseating granulomas** from a **type IV** (T-cell) reaction to beryllium, so it can look like sarcoidosis and may respond to steroids. Exposure: **aerospace**, **electronics** and nuclear industries.
cards.back_pt: **Granulomas não caseosos** por reação **tipo IV** (mediada por linfócitos T) ao berílio; por isso pode simular sarcoidose e pode responder a corticoides. Exposição: indústrias **aeroespacial**, **eletrônica** e nuclear.

cards.front: What causes hypersensitivity pneumonitis, and what are two classic examples?
cards.back: A mixed **type III and type IV** reaction to inhaled **organic antigens**. Examples: **farmer's lung** (thermophilic actinomycetes in moldy hay) and **bird fancier's lung** (bird proteins). Symptoms improve away from the exposure.
cards.back_pt: Reação mista **tipo III e tipo IV** a **antígenos orgânicos** inalados. Exemplos: **pulmão do fazendeiro** (actinomicetos termofílicos em feno mofado) e **pulmão do criador de aves** (proteínas de aves). Os sintomas melhoram longe da exposição.

cards.back: An acute form of **sarcoidosis**: **erythema nodosum**, **bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy**, fever and **ankle arthritis**. It usually resolves on its own and has a good prognosis.
cards.back_pt: Forma aguda de **sarcoidose**: **eritema nodoso**, **linfonodomegalia hilar bilateral**, febre e **artrite/periartrite de tornozelos**. Costuma regredir espontaneamente e tem bom prognóstico.

cards.front: What is the histology of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)?
cards.back: **Diffuse alveolar damage**. Neutrophils injure the alveolar-capillary membrane, and protein-rich fluid leaks into the alveoli. Fibrin and debris from dead type I pneumocytes form **hyaline membranes** that line the alveoli.
cards.back_pt: **Dano alveolar difuso**. Neutrófilos lesam a membrana alvéolo-capilar, e líquido rico em proteínas extravasa para os alvéolos. Fibrina e restos de pneumócitos tipo I mortos formam **membranas hialinas** que revestem os alvéolos.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man comes to the clinic with 2 years of slowly worsening shortness of breath and a dry cough. He has never smoked. For 30 years he worked in a granite quarry and later as a sandblaster. Chest x-ray shows many small nodules in both upper lobes and thin rims of calcification around enlarged hilar lymph nodes. Pulmonary function tests show reduced total lung capacity with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio. This patient has the greatest increase in risk for which of the following conditions?
choices: Malignant pleural mesothelioma
Pneumocystis pneumonia
Pulmonary tuberculosis
Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
Legionnaires disease
questions.explanation: Quarry work and sandblasting, **upper-lobe nodules** and **eggshell calcification** of hilar nodes point to **silicosis**. Silica damages the phagolysosomes of alveolar macrophages, so they kill mycobacteria poorly and the risk of **tuberculosis** rises. Mesothelioma is tied to **asbestos**, which causes lower-lobe fibrosis and pleural plaques, not upper-lobe nodules with eggshell nodes.
questions.explanation_pt: Trabalho em pedreira e com jateamento de areia, **nódulos em lobos superiores** e **calcificação em casca de ovo** dos linfonodos hilares indicam **silicose**. A sílica lesa os fagolisossomos dos macrófagos alveolares, que passam a matar mal as micobactérias, e o risco de **tuberculose** aumenta. O mesotelioma está ligado ao **asbesto (amianto)**, que causa fibrose de lobos inferiores e placas pleurais, e não nódulos em lobos superiores com linfonodos em casca de ovo.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old African American woman has 4 months of dry cough, fatigue and mild shortness of breath. She also reports increased thirst and urination. She does not smoke. Exam shows tender red nodules on both shins. Chest x-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Serum calcium is 11.8 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5), and parathyroid hormone is low. A transbronchial biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas, and stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi are negative. Which mechanism best explains her hypercalcemia?
choices: Secretion of PTH-related peptide by a tumor
Autonomous secretion of parathyroid hormone by a parathyroid adenoma
Osteolytic bone destruction by metastatic cells
Reduced urinary calcium excretion from a thiazide diuretic
Increased 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity in activated granuloma macrophages
questions.explanation: This is **sarcoidosis**. Activated macrophages in the granulomas express **1-alpha-hydroxylase**, which converts 25-hydroxyvitamin D to **calcitriol** without normal control. Calcitriol increases calcium absorption in the gut and bone resorption, and the high calcium suppresses PTH. PTHrP from a tumor also causes hypercalcemia with low PTH, but noncaseating granulomas and bilateral hilar nodes with erythema nodosum fit sarcoidosis, not a cancer.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **sarcoidose**. Os macrófagos ativados dos granulomas expressam **1-alfa-hidroxilase**, que converte 25-hidroxivitamina D em **calcitriol** sem o controle normal. O calcitriol aumenta a absorção intestinal de cálcio e a reabsorção óssea, e o cálcio alto suprime o PTH. O PTHrP de um tumor também causa hipercalcemia com PTH baixo, mas granulomas não caseosos e linfonodos hilares bilaterais com eritema nodoso indicam sarcoidose, e não câncer.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man has 18 months of slowly worsening shortness of breath on exertion and a dry cough. He worked as an accountant and has no pets or hobbies with dust exposure. He has digital clubbing, and fine end-inspiratory crackles that sound like Velcro are heard at both lung bases. Pulmonary function tests show a reduced total lung capacity, an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.88, and a reduced DLCO. CT of the chest shows reticular opacities and honeycombing, most marked in the subpleural regions of the lower lobes. Which finding is most likely on lung biopsy?
choices: Well-formed noncaseating granulomas along lymphatic channels
Patchy fibrosis of different ages with fibroblastic foci beside normal lung
Golden-brown beaded rods within areas of interstitial fibrosis
Hyaline membranes lining the alveolar walls
Alveoli filled with hemosiderin-laden macrophages
questions.explanation: Clubbing, basal **Velcro crackles**, a restrictive pattern with low DLCO and **subpleural basal honeycombing** fit **idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis**. Its histology is **usual interstitial pneumonia**: patchy fibrosis of different ages with **fibroblastic foci** next to normal lung. Noncaseating granulomas suggest **sarcoidosis**, which tends to involve the upper lungs and hilar nodes and rarely causes clubbing. Golden-brown beaded rods (ferruginous bodies) would need asbestos exposure, which he does not have.
questions.explanation_pt: Baqueteamento digital, **estertores em velcro** nas bases, padrão restritivo com DLCO baixa e **faveolamento subpleural basal** indicam **fibrose pulmonar idiopática**. Sua histologia é a **pneumonia intersticial usual**: fibrose em placas, de idades diferentes, com **focos fibroblásticos** ao lado de pulmão normal. Granulomas não caseosos sugerem **sarcoidose**, que tende a acometer os campos superiores e os linfonodos hilares e raramente causa baqueteamento. Bastões castanho-dourados em contas (corpos ferruginosos) exigiriam exposição ao asbesto, que ele não tem.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman is admitted with septic shock from a urinary tract infection. On the second day she becomes very short of breath. Respirations are 34/min, pulse is 118/min, and blood pressure is 104/66 mm Hg. Oxygen saturation is 84% and rises only to 88% with a high-flow oxygen mask. Jugular veins are not distended, and there is no S3. Chest x-ray shows bilateral diffuse alveolar opacities with a normal heart size. Echocardiography shows normal left ventricular function, and the pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is normal. What is the main mechanism of fluid accumulation in her lungs?
choices: Increased pulmonary capillary hydrostatic pressure
Decreased plasma oncotic pressure from protein loss
Obstruction of pulmonary lymphatic drainage
Increased alveolar-capillary permeability from neutrophil-mediated injury
Surfactant deficiency from immature type II pneumocytes
questions.explanation: **Sepsis** is the most common cause of **ARDS**. Neutrophils and cytokines injure the alveolar-capillary membrane, so **protein-rich fluid leaks** into the alveoli: a **noncardiogenic edema** with hyaline membranes. Hypoxemia that barely responds to oxygen reflects shunting through fluid-filled alveoli. **Cardiogenic edema** comes from high capillary hydrostatic pressure, but the normal wedge pressure, normal left ventricle, no S3 and flat neck veins rule it out.
questions.explanation_pt: A **sepse** é a causa mais comum de **SDRA**. Neutrófilos e citocinas lesam a membrana alvéolo-capilar, e **líquido rico em proteínas extravasa** para os alvéolos: um **edema não cardiogênico** com membranas hialinas. A hipoxemia que quase não responde ao oxigênio reflete *shunt* pelos alvéolos cheios de líquido. O **edema cardiogênico** resulta de pressão hidrostática capilar alta, mas a pressão de oclusão da artéria pulmonar (pressão capilar pulmonar) normal, o ventrículo esquerdo normal, a ausência de B3 e a ausência de estase jugular o excluem.

notes.title: Restrictive lung disease: physiology, fibrosis, dust diseases, granulomas and ARDS
notes.body_md:
## Physiology

- **Low TLC**; FEV1 and FVC fall together, so **FEV1/FVC is normal or high**.
- **Intrinsic** (interstitial) disease: stiff lungs, **low DLCO**.
- **Extrinsic** causes: poor breathing mechanics with **normal DLCO**. Examples: **obesity**, **neuromuscular disease** (myasthenia gravis, ALS), **kyphoscoliosis**.

## Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

- Older adults, often smokers; slowly progressive dyspnea, dry cough, **clubbing**, basal **Velcro crackles**.
- **Usual interstitial pneumonia**: patchy fibrosis of different ages, **fibroblastic foci**, **subpleural basal honeycombing**.
- Drugs that cause pulmonary fibrosis: **bleomycin**, **busulfan**, **methotrexate**, **amiodarone**, **nitrofurantoin**.

## Pneumoconioses

- **Coal workers' pneumoconiosis**: **upper lobes**; carbon-laden macrophages. Pneumoconiosis plus **rheumatoid arthritis** gives large rheumatoid nodules in the lungs (**Caplan syndrome**); also seen with silica and asbestos.
- **Silicosis** (quarries, sandblasting, foundries): **upper lobes**, **eggshell calcification** of hilar nodes, **tuberculosis** risk from macrophage dysfunction.
- **Asbestosis** (shipyards, insulation, old buildings): **lower lobes**, **ferruginous bodies**, calcified **pleural plaques**. Higher risk of **bronchogenic carcinoma** and of **mesothelioma**.
- **Berylliosis** (aerospace, electronics): **noncaseating granulomas**; may respond to steroids.

## Immune and granulomatous disease

- **Hypersensitivity pneumonitis**: **type III and IV** reaction to organic antigens (**farmer's lung**, **bird fancier's lung**).
- **Sarcoidosis**: **noncaseating granulomas**, **bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy**, often high **ACE**. Granuloma macrophages make **1-alpha-hydroxylase**, so calcitriol and calcium rise.
- **Löfgren syndrome**: erythema nodosum, hilar nodes, fever, ankle arthritis; good prognosis.
- **Goodpasture syndrome** (anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies): lung hemorrhage plus glomerulonephritis; covered in the renal system.

## ARDS

- Causes: **sepsis**, pneumonia, aspiration, trauma, **pancreatitis**.
- **Diffuse alveolar damage** with **hyaline membranes**; **noncardiogenic edema** with a **normal wedge pressure**.
- Hypoxemia responds poorly to oxygen (shunt).

## Neonatal RDS

- **Surfactant deficiency** in preterm infants causes alveolar collapse and hyaline membranes.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Fisiologia

- **CPT baixa**; VEF1 e CVF caem juntos, então a **relação VEF1/CVF fica normal ou alta**.
- Doença **intrínseca** (intersticial): pulmões rígidos, **DLCO baixa**.
- Causas **extrínsecas**: mecânica respiratória ruim, com **DLCO normal**. Exemplos: **obesidade**, **doença neuromuscular** (miastenia gravis, ELA), **cifoescoliose**.

## Fibrose pulmonar idiopática

- Adultos mais velhos, frequentemente tabagistas; dispneia progressiva e insidiosa, tosse seca, **baqueteamento digital**, **estertores em velcro** nas bases.
- **Pneumonia intersticial usual**: fibrose em placas, de idades diferentes, **focos fibroblásticos**, **faveolamento subpleural basal**.
- Fármacos que causam fibrose pulmonar: **bleomicina**, **bussulfano**, **metotrexato**, **amiodarona**, **nitrofurantoína**.

## Pneumoconioses

- **Pneumoconiose dos mineiros de carvão**: **lobos superiores**; macrófagos carregados de carvão. Pneumoconiose com **artrite reumatoide** produz grandes nódulos reumatoides nos pulmões (**síndrome de Caplan**); também ocorre com sílica e asbesto.
- **Silicose** (pedreiras, jateamento de areia, fundições): **lobos superiores**, **calcificação em casca de ovo** dos linfonodos hilares, risco de **tuberculose** por disfunção dos macrófagos.
- **Asbestose** (exposição ao asbesto/amianto em estaleiros, isolamento térmico, prédios antigos): **lobos inferiores**, **corpos ferruginosos**, **placas pleurais** calcificadas. Risco maior de **carcinoma broncogênico** e de **mesotelioma**.
- **Beriliose** (indústria aeroespacial, eletrônica): **granulomas não caseosos**; pode responder a corticoides.

## Doenças imunes e granulomatosas

- **Pneumonite de hipersensibilidade**: reação **tipo III e IV** a antígenos orgânicos (**pulmão do fazendeiro**, **pulmão do criador de aves**).
- **Sarcoidose**: **granulomas não caseosos**, **linfonodomegalia hilar bilateral**, frequentemente **ECA** elevada. Os macrófagos dos granulomas produzem **1-alfa-hidroxilase**, e o calcitriol e o cálcio sobem.
- **Síndrome de Löfgren**: eritema nodoso, linfonodos hilares, febre, artrite de tornozelos; bom prognóstico.
- **Síndrome de Goodpasture** (anticorpos antimembrana basal glomerular, anti-MBG): hemorragia pulmonar com glomerulonefrite; abordada no sistema renal.

## SDRA

- Causas: **sepse**, pneumonia, aspiração, trauma, **pancreatite**.
- **Dano alveolar difuso** com **membranas hialinas**; **edema não cardiogênico** com **pressão de oclusão da artéria pulmonar (pressão capilar pulmonar) normal**.
- A hipoxemia responde mal ao oxigênio (*shunt*).

## SDR neonatal

- A **deficiência de surfactante** no prematuro causa colapso alveolar e membranas hialinas.
